statement: Frame scheduling may account for more of the handshake measurement than the status IPC round trip.
mechanism: The existing interval ends after a requestAnimationFrame callback, so main-thread scheduling contributes to its duration.
falsifier: In a qualified paired campaign, post-status frame wait is no greater than status IPC in most sessions and the controlled scheduling change does not reduce it.
baseline: Current status invoke plus subsequent frame callback, with additive phase spans.
treatment: Same instrumentation and status semantics; defer only identified unrelated startup UI work until after the callback.
prediction: Post-status frame-wait span decreases while status IPC span and status semantics remain stable.
controls: Same window visibility and refresh mode
required_spans: frontend status response to frame callback

statement: Late prewarm completion or upstream initialization may explain startup delay even when chat_connect itself is short.
mechanism: Native prewarm, process acquisition, bridge startup, initialize and thread/start are distinct intervals; process presence does not imply readiness.
falsifier: Correlated qualified sessions show readiness already emitted before binding, with neither prewarm waiting nor upstream initialization on the launch-to-ready critical path; a scheduling-only prewarm change does not improve that path.
baseline: Current native prewarm placement with process-local spans and launch/session correlation.
treatment: Move only the prewarm scheduling point earlier without reusing a process from a previous desktop session or changing initialization semantics.
prediction: Launch-to-visible-ready decreases if prewarm overlap is limiting; if initialization duration dominates unchanged, that alternative remains open.
controls: Fresh desktop and bridge processes in each arm
required_spans: frontend monotonic connect to ready receive
confounders: OS filesystem caches are not reset by a fresh process

statement: Buffered session.ready delivery may dominate the observed connect-to-ready interval after upstream initialization has finished.
mechanism: Event binding and replay determine when a previously emitted ready event reaches the frontend.
falsifier: Correlated qualified traces show ready is never buffered or replay residence is negligible, and changing replay scheduling alone does not reduce visible-ready latency.
baseline: Existing event bind and replay order with ready-event identity and native buffer-residence spans.
treatment: Prioritize replay immediately after binding, preserving event ordering, deduplication and delivery semantics.
prediction: Native buffer residence and frontend ready-receive delay decrease without reducing upstream initialization duration.
controls: Same ready-event identity across emission, buffering and receipt
required_spans: ready event correlation ID and replay flag

statement: Frontend batching and conditional scrolling may explain delta-to-frame delay independently of upstream delta production.
mechanism: The oldest batched delta anchors the metric, projection is timestamped before scrolling, and paint ends at a frame callback rather than presented pixels.
falsifier: Qualified correlated spans show batching, DOM update and scrolling are small relative to delivery, and coalescing redundant scroll operations does not improve receive-to-frame timing.
baseline: Current batching, DOM update and conditional scrolling with additive frontend spans.
treatment: Coalesce redundant scroll operations within each existing batch while preserving text order and user scroll intent.
prediction: Scroll cost and frontend receive-to-frame decrease without changing content, delta ordering or existing metric definitions.
controls: Same replayable delta stream and essay length
Same viewport and user scroll position
Separate provider runs from deterministic delivery fixtures
confounders: Frame callback is not pixel presentation
